text: Python lockfile admission refuses text pip could read differently from it (#748, refining D-0305): any byte but tab, line feed and printable ASCII once CRLF is normalized, a coding declaration in the first two lines, a whole-line comment ending in a backslash, and a "#" that doesn't start the line or follow whitespace. Admission split lines and stripped comments differently from pip, so a lockfile it accepted could carry a line only pip read, such as --no-binary=:all:, whose source build would run during the networked install. Only base lockfiles were installed until #740's change (#746) installs a pull request's own; an independent review of that change found the gap and confirmed it with real pip. pip-compile and uv output stay admissible. Built by hand to save Codex credits, as D-0331's queue was.
